messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: high-rate CUDA illegal memory access observed on serving-runtime pool 'gpu-1b' (alerts: retries up, tail latency spike). Allocating incident channel.
maria.ops: seeing a burst of OOMs + CUDA illegal-access on 3 nodes in cluster-west-2a. Containers crash with 'illegal memory access' stacks during heavy pagewalks. First customer reports increased 500s. Paging pressure spike around 15:33 UTC.
macros: attaching quick dump
maria.ops: logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T15:33:12Z] runtime.cpp:2145] CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: launch failed
[2026-03-15T15:33:12Z] backtrace: serving_runtime::dispatch -> gpu_kv_cache::get -> pagewalk::translate_offset+0x3f
Container: rwinf/serve:release-2026-03-14
```
.devon-ml: looking. pattern: illegal access happens during long prompt continuity (KVsize > 2GB) and concurrent eviction. sounds like pagewalk + eviction race. can you confirm which model and sequence lengths? @maria.ops
maria.ops: affected pods: serve-v3-abc[0..2], model gpt-open-13b-quant, typical seq ~2048->8192 under burst. KV cache growth observed before crash. Node kernel messages show SMMU page faults.
.taylor-se: customer impact: 3 customers saw 500s, highest QPS route degraded for ~7m. billing logs show spike in retries. We should prepare a customer-safe note; tagging SRE for ETA on mitigation.
sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) cordon+drain affected nodes 2) scale up dedicated pool to shift traffic 3) fallback to quantized smaller model variant (gpt-open-6b) 4) apply hotpatch to disable concurrent eviction for now. Which do we prefer for fastest recovery?
maria.ops: start with cordon+drain, and shifting traffic to spare pool. also immediate route-level fallback to 6b for low-latency routes. we'll do hotpatch if drains don't stop crashes.
.devon-ml: on repro: can reproduce locally with stress harness using long-context replay and interleaved eviction. attaching repro steps:
```
# reproduce harness (simplified)
python tools/repro_eviction.py --model gpt-open-13b-quant --seq 8192 --concurrency 12 --evict-interval 0.2
# watch for cuda error
```
maria.ops: executing cordon/drain on nodes gpu-1b-az2-[12,13,14]
```
kubectl cordon gpu-1b-az2-12
kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-1b-az2-12
```
.sre: draining. routing rule update in progress: canary fallback for route /api/text -> gpt-open-6b on 30% -> will ramp as errors persist. config pushed by routing-bot.
oncall-bot: @maria.ops you are now direct oncall. Hands off in 45m to @devon-ml per rotation.
.devon-ml: will take the deep-dive after drains. immediate ask: get kernel oops from nodes (dmesg + SMMU traces) and capture /proc/pid/maps for crashed containers. Also capture GPU coredump via nvidia-smi dump if available.
maria.ops: collected dmesg excerpt: "gpu: gpu_pagewalk: sgt_misaligned: page table walk returned -EFAULT at 0x7f8b3c000" — sending to devon.
.taylor-se: drafting customer note: short update + ETA. status: degraded routes, mitigations applied (node drain + route fallback), next update in 30m. assigning to me to send after legal review.
.devon-ml: next steps: reproduce with kernel build + instrument pagewalk path; try disabling concurrent eviction + KV snapshotting as we suspect race while freeing page table entries. If hotpatch avoids crashes we can ship a targeted kernel param change. planning a small canary kernel rollout.
maria.ops: post-drain health: error rate down 70%, latency recovering. still monitoring for residual crashes. rolling node replacements continuing.
.sre: marking incident severity: Sev2 -> keep comms cadence 30m. create postmortem ticket and link.
.taylor-se: customer note sent to affected customers, included workaround and ETA. reactions: :thumbsup: from product.
oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: @devon-ml will be oncall owner for next 45m. Incident channel will remain open for any regressions.
maria.ops: leaving notes in the thread: saved core files to s3://redwood-incidents/5932104567/cores, uploaded repro harness. will follow up on next steps for permanent fix (kernel SMMU pagewalk guard + runtime eviction serialization).
.devon-ml: ack — starting root cause triage. will post debug patches and test results in this thread.
sre: closing loop with ops: postmortem owner assigned to @taylor-se. tagging for timeline and action items."
